title: Irresistible
summary: The third consecutive Big Bear episode is an unusually useful lesson in transcript epistemology. Its ordinary first half covers a struggling recreational hockey team, the first Ranch night, Bill Poon's snoring, Steve Lee's masturbation-abstinence promise, Sizzler, a bathroom knock first blamed on a ghost and then traced to Val, a sleep-deprived failed fishing hike, Bobby Lee's gaming and phone fixation, the recurring 'funnier Lee brother' provocation, communal cooking, and the allocation of Ranch bedrooms. After David Choe and Asa Akira truthfully say they talked until sunrise and eventually shared a very large bed with a boundary between them, they spend nearly an hour claiming the encounter became sex. The performance accumulates dry-humping, ejaculation, pregnancy risk, Tony roleplay, guilt, home-wrecking, Cialis, secrecy and responsibility details. Other participants react in real time, some condemning David, some assigning responsibility to Asa, some sexualizing the story, and some remaining skeptical. None of those reactions corroborates the alleged affair. A timestamped text exchange read aloud near the end shows David and Asa planned immediately before recording to tell everyone they had sex and reveal 'JK' at the end. Within Episode 136 they then deny sex and reconstruct the night as conversation, couch/bed logistics, Robocop 2 and sleep. Episode 139 later claims that denial was itself the middle layer of a planned double prank and re-alleges that sex occurred. The archive therefore records a three-state sequence—alleged, denied, re-alleged—rather than declaring either the confession or denial independently verified. Every embedded sexual detail remains attributed to the speakers and later supersession state, never promoted to external fact. This validates a three-layer product design: immutable transcript, claim-level correction/provenance, and interpretation that can change when later evidence arrives. Other meaningful threads include correction of Bobby's claimed honesty with his mother, porn/obscenity-law discussion, private spouse boundaries, the cast's invented racial-code callback, body/food pressure, fertility misinformation explicitly mocked as feelings-based science, and the closing description of the podcast as a diary of changing beliefs. All seventeen cleaner edits are empty records. Automated Sizzler-to-Twizzler substitutions are rejected. Named turns remain unpublished because held-out second-speaker detection failed.
source_notes: All seventeen cleaner edits remove empty records. Raw and clean word counts are identical.

Accept direct show/public-name normalizations including David Choe, Asa/Asa Akira and DVDASA. Reject all five Sizzler → Twizzler edits. Other proposed substitutions require local context; rapid musical-intro names remain partly uncertain.

Within Episode 136, timestamped pre-show texts at about 1:31:35 prove a coordinated confession-and-JK performance, and the hosts deny sex at about 1:33:14. Episode 139 later says that denial was itself a planned second prank and re-alleges sex. The correct corpus state is alleged → denied → re-alleged, not independently resolved.
A claim spoken as confession, repeated by two participants, elaborated for an hour, and reacted to by a room full of people is still not corroborated when all sources share the same staged premise.

Real underlying events are narrower: David and Asa talked all night, discussed sex/incest/porn, eventually shared a large bed with separation, and did not report sex after the reveal. Robocop 2, couch sleeping and a long fart are offered as the mundane ending.
The later 'all details were true except sex' statement is immediately followed by another Tony claim and retraction. The archive records this as nested unreliability, not a stable partial confession.
The title comes from Bobby's reportedly genuine pre-prank reaction that David's weight loss made him 'irresistible.' It does not prove the invented affair.
A private spouse's name, listening practice, health detail and relationship uncertainty are relevant to the prank's ethics but should not become a searchable personal dossier.
The ghost story is internally resolved as a real knock by Val, not paranormal evidence or a murdered Ranch-family history.
Fertility, diet, diabetes, sleep apnea, ADD, linguistics, obscenity law and Sylvester Graham claims are conversational and require independent verification before factual reuse.
speaker_policy: Public participants are identifiable at episode level through the introduction and direct address, but zero validated turns/windows means no line-level names. This episode especially forbids inferring speaker truthfulness or identity from narrative consistency: two public hosts knowingly coordinate a false confession, while other voices merely react to it.
